newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up on strong December growth.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up on strong December growth.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Tuesday as December's year-on-year gross domestic growth of 8.5 percent, signalling likley solid economic growth this year, encouraged investors to buy equities, brokers said.
They added that confidence economic development would result in good company profits would motivate players to buy again on Wednesday and push the market up further.
On Tuesday, the General Index .IGRA rose 1.81 percent to 1,574.0 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL rose 1.84 percent to 2,269.1.

During the session, the National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said that year-on-year GDP rose 8.5 percent in December 1996, compared with a 1.7 percent year-on-year contraction in the same month in 1995.
The December figure meant the economy grew 2.8 percent in 1996, compared with 7.0 percent in 1995, the INEI added.

"The production figure was stronger than many expected and so investors immediately positioned themselves in companies that produce for mass consumption and in breweries and cement companies," said Augusto Lafora of the local brokerage Prisma.
In a total of 1,915 trades, 63 stocks rose, 19 fell and one stock remained unchanged. Volume was 29.4 million soles ($11.1 million).
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 2.98 percent to 5.88 soles on volume of 1.91 million shares, while brewery Backus y Johnston rose 6.82 percent to 2.35 soles on volume of 1.27 million shares.
The brewery sector in general rose 4.14 percent, brokers said.
